method: Read-only survey of the working tree, with no web or external factual sources. Recursively enumerated all files with Markdown extensions, including hidden-directory pages, repository documentation, includes, archives and reference stubs: 1,218 pages. Inventoried titles, headings, opening text, lengths and include relationships; inspected representative bodies and searched for exact repeated paragraphs and related explanations. Grouped by reader task, product ownership, shared page templates and structural workload. Target structures follow STYLE.md and COMPONENTS.md: clear openings, content-type-appropriate headings, prerequisites/steps/verification where warranted, and links to shared explanations. Snippets, navigation stubs, reference tables and release histories retain their specialized forms. The 90-minute estimates assume template-based structural changes with technical bodies preserved; they do not establish full-rewrite feasibility. Directory paths ending in / cover all descendant Markdown files; other paths identify individual pages. Programmatic validation confirmed 25 areas, page counts summing to 1,218, exactly one owner per page, and no unmatched path entries. Trunk page lists identify observed repetition candidates rather than exhaustive occurrence lists; all listed source pages exist. Fifteen proposed trunk paths reuse existing pages and seven propose new pages. No files were edited.

rationales.A01: Documentation authoring and discovery: repository guidance, templates, landing pages and general snippets. A bounded pass can align authoring guidance, navigation and reusable-notice formats.
rationales.A02: Beginner foundations and workshop form one learning sequence. Reuse explanation/practice/next-step structures and shared fundamentals while preserving exercises.
rationales.A03: JavaScript and browser application guides share containerize/develop/test/CI/deploy chapter patterns. One series template supports batch normalization while retaining framework-specific examples.
rationales.A04: Other language and framework guides follow the same development lifecycle. Batch common chapter structures and prerequisite links; preserve language-specific Dockerfiles, commands and application code.
rationales.A05: Testcontainers tutorials and dependency-testing recipes repeat short create-project/write-tests/run-tests series. Their shared template makes structural batching practical; integration-specific tests remain intact.
rationales.A06: Application recipes, data services, observability and sample discovery. Forty-two pages are mostly tiny sample-catalog stubs; remaining recipes can share prerequisites/run/connect/verify/cleanup structures.
rationales.A07: AI models, agents and application development. Normalize setup/configure/run/verify sections and shared inference prerequisites; preserve model settings, agent configurations and application examples.
rationales.A08: AI tool connections and isolated workspaces: MCP profiles/gateway, sandbox agents and workflow tutorials. Shared setup and agent-page templates support a bounded pass while preserving credential and isolation distinctions.
rationales.A09: Image construction, cache, outputs, metadata and build policy. Align concept, task and reference wrappers and link shared build fundamentals; retain examples and policy definitions.
rationales.A10: Build execution and automation: builders, Bake, BuildKit, CI and Build Cloud. Batch driver/workflow structures and shared authentication/cache links; preserve workflow code and release payloads.
rationales.A11: Compose user workflows, installation, quickstart and Bridge. Apply focused how-to structures and canonical specification links across environment, watch, file-composition and production tasks.
rationales.A12: Compose specification pages and their source fragments stay together. Normalize reference openings, examples and anchors while preserving attribute tables and specification semantics.
rationales.A13: Desktop installation and lifecycle support. Reuse platform-install and symptom/diagnosis/solution structures while preserving OS permissions, requirements and incident-specific remedies.
rationales.A14: Desktop daily use and runtime features, including WSL, networking, Kubernetes and Offload. Align task openings, settings references and verification links while retaining feature-specific behavior.
rationales.A15: Release history, lifecycle, retirement and security advisories. The bounded target covers archival headers, date/version navigation and shared notices; historical release bodies retain their chronology and content.
rationales.A16: Engine installation and runtime administration. Batch installation/configuration templates and common verification steps; preserve distribution commands, daemon options and resource-management examples.
rationales.A17: Engine data paths and observability. Networking, storage and logging drivers support parallel purpose/configuration/example/limitations structures, with technical tables and advanced examples preserved.
rationales.A18: Engine trust and clustered deployment: host/container protection, rootless operation, content trust and Swarm. Align concept/configuration/tutorial wrappers and shared cluster prerequisites; retain security and service examples.
rationales.A19: Hub repositories, publishing, trusted programs, usage and registry APIs. Apply repository-task and API-lifecycle templates; preserve analytics definitions and endpoint-specific content.
rationales.A20: Scout analysis, remediation, policy and integrations. Repeated analysis/integration patterns support common setup, authentication, verification and removal structures.
rationales.A21: Hardened Images concepts and adoption. Reuse concept and migration templates and shared supply-chain definitions; retain compliance guarantees, image-specific instructions and migration examples.
rationales.A22: Accounts, organizations and commerce: identity, membership, subscriptions, seats, billing and support. Apply common access/prerequisite/task structures and shared role/licensing explanations.
rationales.A23: Enterprise deployment and policy: managed installers, SSO/provisioning, roles and hardened Desktop controls. Align configure/verify/troubleshoot structures; preserve settings tables and rollout-specific steps.
rationales.A24: Extensions development and API reference. Batch tutorial and interface templates, consolidate SDK setup/execution explanations, and preserve signatures, architecture and publishing examples.
rationales.A25: Engine API and SDK integration. Most pages are short version wrappers; apply one wrapper template and align SDK setup/examples while preserving version identifiers.

trunk_inventory.topic: Common tutorial prerequisites: Docker Desktop, Git and basic Docker knowledge. Centralize setup; retain project-specific versions and clone URLs.
docker init scaffolding: purpose, generated files and generic build/run verification. Keep language-specific prompt responses local.
GitHub Actions build/publish setup: Hub token, repository variables/secrets, login/build-push actions and publication checks. Reuse the generic guide and reconcile secret-name variants.
Local Kubernetes deployment cycle: Desktop Kubernetes, Deployment/NodePort manifests, apply/get/browser checks and delete cleanup. Keep application images and ports local.
Compose Watch development loop: watch configuration, automatic rebuild/sync and --watch startup. Retain framework reload commands and ignored paths.
Testcontainers introduction and common Docker runtime prerequisites. Reuse the product overview; retain language libraries and integration-specific fixtures.

Common Engine installation steps: conflicting packages, hello-world verification, non-root setup, convenience-script caveats and uninstall data cleanup. Keep distribution package/repository commands local; install-script.md already shares part of this.
Persistent data and volume lifecycle: surviving container replacement, named volumes versus bind mounts and database persistence. Retain database paths, permissions and UI tasks.
Port publishing fundamentals: host/container ports, -p/ports mapping and localhost access. Keep firewall behavior and platform limitations local.
Compose networking fundamentals: default network, service-name DNS and container versus host access. Keep connection strings and platform-specific host access in recipes.
Build layers/cache: reuse, invalidation, dependency-first COPY ordering and .dockerignore. Share core explanations; retain backend-specific exports.
Multi-stage builds: separate build/test/runtime stages, copy final artifacts and select named targets. Retain compiler, dependency and hardened-image details.
SBOM concepts: component/dependency inventory, versions/licenses, vulnerability analysis and SBOM versus attestation. Centralize definitions; retain generation, verification and DHI guarantees.
Image attestations/provenance: contents/build-origin metadata, signatures and supply-chain policy. Centralize definitions; distinguish BuildKit modes, CI defaults and DHI signed guarantees.
VEX versus raw CVE counts: exploitability statements, statuses, justifications and scanner filtering. Retain Scout exception handling, DHI conventions and scanner-specific behavior.

Model Runner connectivity: host TCP, host/container base URLs, compatible API paths, placeholder keys and endpoint checks. Expand the API URL reference; retain client-specific configuration and compatibility notes.
MCP profiles: named server collections, catalog selection, adding servers, client connections and gateway execution. Reuse the profile explanation; retain GUI/CLI procedures.
Sandbox credentials: stored secrets, environment variables, proxy injection and host-side isolation. Retain provider names and API-key/OAuth differences on agent pages.
Organization/team roles: owners versus members, invitations, role assignment and repository access. Centralize definitions; retain company/org UI differences, seat effects and provisioning.
Desktop licensing: repeated commercial-use thresholds, paid-subscription requirements and terms. Reuse the license page and notice; retain platform installation requirements.

Image-store capabilities: containerd versus classic storage, multi-platform manifests, attestation preservation and custom-builder push/load behavior. Keep Engine/Desktop enablement differences local.
Extension command execution: Docker/VM/host contexts, asynchronous results, streaming callbacks and process lifetime. Reuse the backend guide; retain interface signatures and V0 behavior.
